object_description: five-building school ensemble linked by a linear promenade
design_condition: The buildings confirm and extend the existing structure, closing the complex to the east and arranging differentiated open spaces along a linear promenade that responds to the terrain and surrounding settlement.

positive.statement: The project creates a simple and coherent spatial arrangement with a well-proportioned sequence of open spaces.
The differentiated urban development establishes a stable order while relating carefully to the topographical structure.
The simple floor plans are suitable for use and do justice to everyday school life.
The linear promenade connects the buildings and makes the complex appear clear from an operational perspective.
The comparable structural grid provides a high degree of flexibility for later adjustments.
The architectural expression is pleasantly unspectacular, while the constructive implementation is coherent and creates identity.
The project largely meets sustainability requirements through its careful use of resources.

negative.statement: The open-space design remains fragmentary, rudimentary and schematic, without realizing the potential for specific atmospheres.
The urban-development and open-space approach has significant deficiencies in level transitions and accessibility for protection and rescue.
The mixing of delivery and main access is not cleverly chosen.
The grass playing field cannot be convincingly integrated into the local topography.
The southern parking areas are questionable in relation to the proposed green concept.
The classroom window openings are too large and risk excessive heat input on the west and south sides.
